$note: Machine-readable pin records for every ABSOLUTE bundle budget in this repo (plan-779).
One file, because the three guards that defend the startup path had drifted apart:
printed the demo entry WITHOUT any budget at all, and `bundle-eager-imports.node.test.ts`
walked the eager source graph without ever summing it. The prose history of the dist
entry stays where it is (the ENTRY_BUDGET_BYTES comment in bundle-splitting.test.ts) —
only the numbers and their PROVENANCE live here, so that one test can check all of them.
THE RULE, learned twice the hard way (08.08.2026 and again 22.10.2026):
an absolute budget is pinned ONLY from a build of the MERGE TARGET. A number measured on
a feature branch is a number measured on a tree the trunk does not have: on 22.10.2026 the
dist entry was pinned at 4_866_000 from fedb6670 (feature/plan-652-lazy-feature-plugins),
2 h 20 min AFTER the path-network planner UI had been merged to main — `git merge-base
--is-ancestor bf533461 fedb6670` says no, so ~54 kB that already sat on the trunk were
missing from the measurement. The budget was over on the day it was written.
WHOEVER CHANGES A NUMBER HERE fills in `measuredAt` truthfully: the commit the measurement
was taken at, and whether that commit sits on the merge target. The commit is not decoration
— `bundle-budget-provenance.node.test.ts` runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor` on it and fails
when the answer is no. That is the convention standing in the way instead of being documented.

Tolerance 150_153 B (0.95 %) above the measurement, which is ONE median day of trunk
growth, not a noise band. The honest reason, measured rather than assumed: the eager
this guard has to catch are +221_407, +363_333, +93_287 and +153_530 B — i.e. the SMALLEST
of them is smaller than an ordinary day on this trunk. No single absolute threshold can
therefore both pass a normal week and fail every cluster; a tight one is the only variant
that guards anything, so this one is tight and WILL trip every few days. Each trip is real
growth of the startup path and the cheapest moment to decide lazy-vs-eager. If that cadence
is unwanted, the fix is a per-change guard (eager delta against the merge-base, which needs
no build either), NOT a bigger number — see the report for plan-779.
Cross-machine note: the walk measures the WORKTREE, so a checkout with different EOL
settings reads ~28 kB differently (measured: git-archive tree vs this worktree). That is
inside the tolerance, but it is the reason the tolerance cannot be a few kB.
